topics.title: Inflation remains a kitchen-table concern
topics.summary: U.S. inflation accelerated to 3.7% last month, driven by higher gasoline, clothing and airfare costs. The report keeps everyday prices at the center of economic conversations.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your usual groceries, clothes, or travel suddenly cost more, what is the first small luxury you would protect anyway?

topics.title: Press-access ruling favors news outlets
topics.summary: A federal judge extended an order blocking the White House from barring reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico, finding the outlets are likely to succeed on constitutional claims.
topics.discussionPrompt: Should access rules for reporters be the same for every outlet, even when the questions get uncomfortable?

topics.title: Black Sea ship attacks investigated
topics.summary: Bulgaria said Russia was likely behind recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea, while acknowledging the claim could not yet be proved.
topics.discussionPrompt: When officials say something is likely but not proven, how much should people trust the first explanation?

topics.title: Saudi energy offices reportedly struck
topics.summary: Officials said Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Aramco executive offices, adding to regional tensions and raising fresh questions about energy security.
topics.discussionPrompt: When energy news heats up overseas, do you think about fuel prices first, diplomacy first, or neither?

topics.title: Ukraine power concerns continue
topics.summary: Reports said Russian strikes damaged power facilities in Ukraine, leaving many people without electricity as arguments over a possible ceasefire continue.
topics.discussionPrompt: What everyday habit would be hardest to adjust if your neighborhood suddenly lost power for a day?

topics.title: Thailand park closes after floods
topics.summary: Thailand's oldest amusement park closed after flooding damaged rides and left parts of the site inaccessible, highlighting how rising water can disrupt familiar local landmarks.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your favorite old amusement park had to close for repairs, which ride or snack stand would you miss most?

topics.title: Wildlife photos celebrate odd moments
topics.summary: Winners of the 2026 Wildlife Photographer of the Year competition showcased scenes from underwater life to city wildlife, giving nature fans plenty of memorable images to compare.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather photograph a rare animal in the wild or a hilarious everyday creature right in town?

topics.title: Formula 1 eyes Africa return
topics.summary: BBC World Service programming highlighted Formula 1's planned return to Africa, renewing conversation about the sport's global reach and what a new race weekend could bring.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a major race came to your region, would you be there for the cars, the atmosphere, or the food vendors?

topics.title: AI safety enters security debate
topics.summary: The UK's intelligence chief warned about the possible misuse of AI in biological threats, bringing fresh attention to how powerful tools should be developed and safeguarded.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is one sensible rule you would want before powerful new AI tools become ordinary household tech?

topics.title: Data centers keep reshaping debate
topics.summary: A BBC technology program examined the idea of virtual data centers in space, while AI infrastructure continues to prompt questions about energy, cost and future computing.
topics.discussionPrompt: If data centers someday moved into space, what would surprise you more: the engineering, the price tag, or the sci-fi vibes?
